summary: Reviewed 3 artifacts (ShellViewModel.cs, ShellViewModelTests.cs, VideoIndexer.Tests.csproj). Full OWASP Top 10 review completed. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 3 Low findings. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A07 — Identification & Authentication Failures | LOW | File: src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/ShellViewModel.cs, LogOnAsync method. LogOnAsync can be called repeatedly from the LoggingOn state with incorrect passwords — there is no failed-attempt counter, lockout, or delay after N consecutive failures. For a local desktop application this is low risk (attacker requires physical access), but a bounded retry counter at the ShellViewModel or IPasswordService level would improve defence in depth. Remediation: Implement a configurable MaxAttempts counter; after N failures, transition to Error state and require a DisconnectAsync/reconnect to reset.

A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring Failures | LOW | File: src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/ShellViewModel.cs, Transition() and orchestration methods. No ILogger is injected; authentication failures in LogOnAsync (wrong password, verified == false) and all catch-block exceptions are captured silently into LastError with no log output. Failed authentication events are security-significant and should be logged (at Warning level, without logging the supplied password). Remediation: Inject ILogger<ShellViewModel> and log failed VerifyAsync outcomes and caught exceptions at Warning or Error level.

A02 / Data Handling | LOW | File: src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/ShellViewModel.cs, LogOnAsync(string password) and SetPasswordAsync(string password). Password is accepted as a plain .NET string, which is an immutable heap object that cannot be zeroed after use. GC finalization timing means the plaintext password may linger in managed heap memory. For a local desktop app this is a very low practical risk, but accepting ReadOnlySpan<char> or using a char[] that is explicitly cleared would improve security hygiene. Remediation: Change signature to accept ReadOnlySpan<char> or a char[] that callers zero after the call; propagate the pattern to IPasswordService.
